title: Money: Coins and Notes (KS1)
subject: Maths
strapline: Recognising UK coins and notes and making amounts.
facts: 100 pence (100p) is the same as one pound (£1).
You can make the same amount in different ways: 10p = 5p + 5p = 10 × 1p.
To pay for something, you can combine coins to reach the price.
Change is the money you get back when you pay more than the price.
The pound sign £ goes before the number; pence uses p after the number.

quick_quiz.q: You pay 50p for a 30p pencil. How much change?

teacher_tips: Use real or realistic coins — screen images hide the size/weight cues children use.
Play shop with real prices so combining and change have a purpose.
Start with exact amounts before moving on to giving change.
